article.title: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
article.summary:
The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.
"Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy.
It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War".
It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France.
It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened.

article.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
article.summary:
Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

Huang sent a companywide email on Sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation.

article.title: Regret Paying $162 to Upgrade to Premium Class on Alaska Airlines
article.summary:
When I first booked a flight from New York City to Portland, Oregon, on Alaska Airlines for a friend's wedding, I went for the cheapest fare in coach — no changes, no seat selection, and last to board.
Then, I started writing about Alaska Airlines' — and the broader airline industry's — push to attract more premium customers.
Curious about this trend — and tempted by a $162 upgrade offered at check-in for my flight — I decided to test Alaska's current "Premium Class" product.
The upgrade from Main Cabin cost nearly as much as the flight itself.
It came with some perks, including early boarding and extra legroom, but I quickly realized Alaska's "Premium Class" still felt like an extra-legroom economy seat — not the elevated cabin the name had led me to picture.
